jurisdictions.name: St. Charles County (unincorporated)
jurisdictions.office: Community Development, Building and Code Enforcement Division
notes: St. Charles County's Residential Building Permit covers swimming pools, hot tubs and pool barriers on residentially zoned property, applied for in the Citizenserve portal.
Applicants submit the contractor names, building plans (PDF preferred) and a detailed plot plan showing the structure on the lot with distances to property lines.
The county says structures may not be located over easements or septic systems, and at least one inspection is required.
The county separately licenses pool installers through the Citizenserve portal, with a bond and liability insurance certificate.

sources.title: Pool Installers License Application/Renewal (St. Charles County)

jurisdictions.name: Springfield / Greene County
notes: Springfield's swimming pool page covers outdoor private pools, including in-ground pools, hot tubs and spas, and says the pool barrier rules come from the International Building Code.
The city lists a barrier at least 48 inches above finished ground level, with no opening that passes a 4 inch sphere.
Pedestrian gates must open outward away from the pool and be self-closing and self-latching.
Springfield requires an approved building permit before any new one- or two-family house or accessory building is built, and the plans must include a site plan drawn to scale.

jurisdictions.name: Wentzville / St. Charles County
notes: Wentzville lists a Swimming Pool/Hot Tub Permit among the work that needs a building permit.
Since February 23, 2026, all building permit applications go through the SmartGov Permit Portal, and the city no longer accepts paper plan submittals.
The city says it has adopted the 2021 IBC, 2021 IRC and 2021 IPC, plus the 2020 National Electrical Code, with local amendments.
Contractors, general and sub, must hold a city-issued contractor's license.

jurisdictions.name: Lake Saint Louis / St. Charles County
jurisdictions.office: Building Division, City of Lake Saint Louis
notes: Lake Saint Louis takes building permit applications and plans through its Citizenserve portal and publishes a pool requirement checklist.
The checklist asks for a site plan at 1 inch = 20 feet prepared by a licensed engineer or surveyor, with easements, elevations, proposed pool rim elevation and drainage contours.
The checklist also asks for the proposed pool barrier details, self-closing outward-swinging gates, door alarms, an erosion control plan, and equipment location with screening.
Contractors must hold a City Business License before doing construction work in the city.

sources.title: Building Permits (City of Lake Saint Louis)
Swimming Pool Requirement Checklist (City of Lake Saint Louis)

jurisdictions.name: Kansas City (Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass Counties)
notes: Kansas City's Information Bulletin No. 119 says a permit is required to build any above-ground or in-ground residential swimming pool, hot tub or spa. A temporary inflatable pool is exempt. So is a prefabricated above-ground pool at a one- or two-family home with walls entirely above grade, a fill level less than 24 inches and a capacity of 5,000 gallons or less. All code requirements still apply without a permit.

The bulletin says pool permits for one- and two-family homes must be submitted online through CompassKC. The site plan must be drawn to scale or on the mortgage survey or recorded subdivision plat. It must show the property line dimensions, the existing home, the pool's dimensions and its distances to the home, other structures and the side and rear property lines. It must also show the required 4-foot-tall fencing, a note on the notification alarms and the overhead or underground electrical service-drop conductors running to the house.

In residential zoning districts, the bulletin says pools may go only in the side or rear yard. They must be at least 10 feet from the side yard property lines and not within a dedicated easement. A pool 10 feet or closer to any building may be subject to a structural plan review.

The bulletin says its pool requirements are found in the Kansas City Zoning and Development Code, Chapter 18 (the Kansas City Building & Rehabilitation Code) and the 2018 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code as amended. It says pools, spas and hot tubs with a fill level greater than 2 feet must be enclosed by a protective fence at least 4 feet high with self-closing, self-latching gates. A lockable cover is accepted instead of the fence on a spa or hot tub. Above-ground pool walls 4 feet or higher may serve as the enclosure. Electrical and plumbing work need separate supplemental permits.

jurisdictions.name: Lee's Summit (Jackson and Cass Counties)
notes: Lee's Summit says permits are required for swimming pools, whether above ground or in-ground. The city's pool handout defines a pool as holding more than 5,000 gallons of water or being more than 24 inches deep at its deepest level.

The city says to email devtech@cityofls.net a Scope of Work Statement, a fencing acknowledgment signed by the homeowner and a surveyed plot plan. The plot plan must show the proposed pool's location and dimensions. It must also show the distances from the closest part of the pool to the rear and side property lines, and the deck around the pool, whether concrete or wood.

The city's pool handout says the pool area must be entirely enclosed by a fence or other permanent structure at least 4 feet high, measured from grade. A 4-inch sphere must not pass through it, and gates need self-closing and self-latching devices at the top. An above-grade structure 4 feet or taller with a ladder that can be lifted and locked does not need the enclosure, but the ladder must be locked when the pool is not attended. A hot tub may have a latching protective cover instead, but a pool in the same area must still be fenced.

The city says Development Services staff will have the plot plan reviewed for property line setbacks. For in-ground pools only, Public Works must also check utility easement setbacks. The handout says the pool cannot be located within any easements, and every inspection needs one day of advance notice. The city says it has adopted the 2024 International Residential Code and the 2023 National Electrical Code, which are now in effect.
